content.title: What is Synchronization?
content.description: Synchronization is a mechanism in Java that controls access to shared resources, ensuring that only one thread executes a critical section of code at a time to prevent data inconsistency.

content.content: In multithreaded applications, multiple threads may access the same resource simultaneously. Without proper synchronization, this can lead to inconsistent results known as race conditions. Java provides the synchronized keyword to ensure thread-safe access to shared resources.

content.title: Why Synchronization?
content.content: Synchronization prevents race conditions, ensures data consistency, and enables safe communication between multiple threads accessing shared resources.
If two or more threads modify the same object simultaneously, unexpected results may occur. Synchronization ensures that only one thread accesses the critical section at any given time.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Synchronization protects the critical section of code where shared data is read or modified.

content.content: A race condition occurs when multiple threads update shared data simultaneously, causing unpredictable and incorrect results.

content.title: Common Problem
content.content: Race conditions occur only when threads share mutable data without proper synchronization.
Marking an entire method as synchronized ensures that only one thread can execute that method on a particular object at a time.

content.content: A synchronized block locks only a specific portion of code, improving performance by minimizing the locked section.

content.title: Synchronization Cost
content.time_complexity: Lock acquisition is generally O(1), but waiting time depends on contention

items.answer: Prevent multiple users from updating the same account simultaneously.

items.answer: Ensure stock quantities remain accurate when multiple orders are processed.

items.question: Reservation Systems
items.answer: Avoid double booking of seats, rooms, or tickets.

items.question: Shared Caches
items.answer: Protect shared data structures from concurrent modifications.

content.title: Single ATM Machine
content.content: Imagine multiple people waiting to use one ATM. Only one person can use it at a time while others wait. Once the current user finishes, the next person gets access. Synchronization works similarly by allowing only one thread into the critical section.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Synchronization, race conditions, critical sections, object locks, class locks, synchronized methods, synchronized blocks, deadlocks, and thread safety are among the most frequently asked Java multithreading interview topics.

items.question: Should every method be synchronized?
items.answer: No. Synchronize only code that accesses shared mutable data to avoid unnecessary performance overhead.

items.question: Does synchronization completely eliminate concurrency?
items.answer: No. Only the synchronized section is protected while other independent code can execute concurrently.

items.question: Can synchronization prevent deadlocks?
items.answer: No. Incorrect lock ordering can still lead to deadlocks.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Synchronization ensures that only one thread executes a critical section at a time, preventing race conditions and maintaining data consistency.
